processors.name: PutDatabaseRecord
processors.comments:
Populate Bridge Table: Inserts the linked relationship into global.Movie_Genres.

Key: Uses the composite key (title, year, genre_name).
Deduplication: Relies on Database Primary Key constraints to reject duplicate associations (Success/Failure relationships are auto-terminated).

processors.name: LookupRecord
processors.comments:
Resolve Foreign Keys: Uses the movie_id from the incoming CSV to query the global.Movies table via the DatabaseRecordLookupService.

Action: Merges the returned title and year directly into the root of the record (Result RecordPath: /).
Purpose: Prepares the data for the bridge table, which uses (title, year) as the Foreign Key, not the ID.

processors.name: PutDatabaseRecord
processors.comments:
Populate Dictionary: Inserts unique genre names into the global.Genres table.

Logic: Uses INSERT_IGNORE to handle duplicates automatically.
Config: Set to Ignore Unmatched Columns so it safely skips the movie_id field, which belongs in the bridge table, not here.

processors.name: LookupRecord
processors.comments:
Given that some records from the previous UpdateRecord may contains some actors that was not included in the DB due to both birth and deathYear missing, we add this extra step to look forward them in the Actors table of the DB, previously filled by another flow.
If not found we manage them so the PutDatabaseRecord will not trigger error for the foreign key missing, due to the actor missing.

processors.name: LookupRecord
processors.comments:
Previous Processor process the bridge dataset from the file: tmdb_5000_credits.csv.
This bridge dataset has columns: ['movie_id', 'actor_name'].
This processor have to lookup from the Movies table and get "title" and "year" values and put them in the nested JSON "movie_info".
Anyway, the RecordReader have a schema for which "title" and "year" are also present in the base JSON as nulls, that because the next UpdateRecord copy data from the nested to those keys, in this way we flatten the JSON and it is ready for Database Load.

processors.name: PutDatabaseRecord
processors.comments:
Load Movies: Inserts the reconciled movie records into global.Movies.

Config: Unmatched Column Behavior is set to Ignore, allowing the database to handle missing columns (filling them with NULLs) for movies that lack financial data.

processors.name: LookupRecord
processors.comments:
Data Fusion (Lookup): Enriches the TMDB data by querying the Secondary Source (BoxOffice CSV) via CSVRecordLookupService.

Key: Matches movies by title.
Result: Inserts the entire Box Office record into a nested field /box_office_data for downstream processing. (Works for every film, both box_office null and not null)

processors.name: UpdateRecord
processors.comments:
JSON Records without Revenue data goes here. (box_office key value null).

Given that box_office is null, we update the record by including at root the keys revenue_domestic and profit, both set initially at null at we rename the column revenue to revenue_worldwide.

processors.name: FetchFile
processors.comments: Retrieve Content: Reads the CSV content. Uses a Schema that treats IDs and Years as Strings initially to prevent type coercion errors from raw Pandas output.

processors.name: QueryRecord
processors.comments: Check that, for each record, year key value is not null, otherwise it cannot be used as primary key in the DB and cause error. Movies for which this value is missing are discarded. Only Movies with valid title, year columns are allowed, given that these are used as PK.

properties.valid_records: SELECT * FROM FLOWFILE WHERE "year" IS NOT NULL
